Act, Satara, rejecting the application filed by the Appellant for grant of bail in connection with C.R. No.1360 of 2023 registered with Phaltan Police Station (Rural) District-Satara, for offences ___Page No.1 of 13___ 24 July 2024 Megha 37_apeal_346_2024-fc.docx punishable under Sections 323, 342, 343, 506, 376 and 376 (D) of the IPC, Sections 3(1)(w)(i), 3(2)(w)(ii), 3(2)(v), 3(1)(h) of the SCST Act and Sections 16, 17 and 18 of the Bonded Labour System (Abolition ) Act, 1976.

If Appellant had any ill-intention towards complainant, he would not take care of her children by admitting them in school.
texts.arguments: vi) That the claim of some labourers about hearing alleged threats of Appellant appear to be unbelievable as none of them bothered to even enquire about complainant after the alleged incident. viii) That despite prolonged custodial interrogation of Appellant, police have not been able to identify or trace the so called accomplices of Appellant, thereby making the entire story of gangrape wholly unbelievable. x) That Appellant's harsh treatment to the labourers in general and he slapping Complainant's husband, in particular, could be the reason for his false implication in the incident. xi) That there are no criminal antecedents against Appellant. xii) That the Appellant has been in custody for more than one year and considering the fact that the trial is not likely to be concluded in near future, the Appellant deserves to be released on bail. That the neighbours were terrified on account of Appellant's threats and were well aware of his capacity to execute such threats since he was in the habit of thrashing any labourer, their family members if they failed to act as per his desire. That this is clear case of Complainant and her family being lured to work with Appellant, the family being held to ransom by illegally keeping complainant's children in custody and thereby committing the heinous crime of gang rape by locking complainant's husband in his house.

Complainant's mother-in- law has stated in her statement given to the police on 8 July 2023 that she heard Appellant threatening other labourers not to come out of their hutments.

True it is that in the statement recorded under Section 164, she has not repeated all the statements made on 8 July 2023.

She has further stated that Appellant threatened all the labourers and their families not to come out of the huts.
Thus, presence of Appellant at the spot of the incident, as well as he giving threats to other labourers is clearly vouched by the mother-in-law even in her statement under Section 164.
